free_tier.stated: No account and no published total quota — storage is per-object and unbounded in count. 'Up to 256 GB per single file. No limit on batch uploads as long as each file is under 256 GB.'

retention.stated: Retention: 'Uploaded files are kept for at least 365 days

egress.terms: Unmetered. 'No speed limits. Speeds depend solely on your network bandwidth. We don't impose any artificial throttling.' Downloads served from Cloudflare with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`.

tooling: Undocumented but fully functional chunked HTTP API, reverse-engineered from the site's own uploader JS: `POST https://u1.bigfile.net/v1/upload` with header `Content-Range: start-end`, header `Hash: <sha256 of whole file encoded base62, left-padded to 43 chars>`, raw body = the chunk; response `{"status":true,"uri":"/d/<base62hash>"}`. Read path: `GET https://www.bigfile.net/d/<base62hash>` (direct octet-stream), plus `GET /d/<hash>/list.json` for multi-file shares. Uploader parallelises across `u1..uN.bigfile.net`. No rclone backend.
chaining: Account-less, so unlimited uploads per IP x 256 GB per object. Chain = N objects x 256 GB with 365-day sliding retention.

limits.value: Retention: 'Uploaded files are kept for at least 365 days

limits_note: per-object-cap 256 GB. Retention: 'Uploaded files are kept for at least 365 days. Files that have not been downloaded for more than 365 days will be automatically deleted' — a sliding window, not a hard expiry, so a monthly GET sweep keeps everything alive indefinitely. No auth, no rate limit observed: 4 concurrent ranged GETs all returned 200 in 1.7-3.3 s.
reliability_note: Genuinely good for a no-account host: upload and read both verified by SHA-256, and the site advertises a 'zero-database architecture' meaning no inventory to lose. The risk is the opposite of the usual one — there is no account, so nobody can enumerate or restore your corpus if you lose the hashes.
confidence_note: The page states the number in the record; the claim is documented, not measured.
